steps.content: Ting-a-ling! Ting-a-ling!
A crisp noise grabs your attention. Instinctively, you shift your focus to the ringing sound, when a gentle, serene voice reaches your ears.
Ms. Martina, are you home? I've got your letter!
Yes, I hear you! I'm right here! ...Yes, yes. Mind your step now, slow down. No rush to get down the stairs...

steps.speaker: Elderly Woman
steps.content: Oh, my dear Dove, what luck you bring me! You're here so early. You must be exhausted. Come on in and rest for a bit, sweetheart?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: That's so kind of you, Martina, but I can't stay. Got my hands full, so I've got to go!
Ting-a-ling! Ting-a-ling!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Oh, Mr. Philippe! No need to come all the way here! Your letter just went out a few days ago. Just be patient, would you?

steps.speaker: Philippe
steps.content: Huh? So none of these letters are for me? Who are they for, then?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Quite a few are for those who've moved to DisCity. They stay with me, though. I'm still looking for someone who can take them to DisCity, to deliver them properly.

steps.speaker: Philippe
steps.content: That's your job too? That sounds like a lot of work! Mind if I say, you should cut yourself some slack!

steps.speaker: Philippe
steps.content: Those folks who've gone to DisCity must be over the moon by now! They've prolly forgotten they ever wrote those letters! I'm so green with envy, I tell ya!

steps.speaker: Curious Local
steps.content: That's right! You know Sheila, the girl who lived down that alley? She just moved to the city a few days ago. Boy, ain't she lucky? Dove, did you know about this? If you'd known earlier, you could've asked her to give you a hand!

steps.speaker: Philippe
steps.content: Look, not everyone's as nice as our lil Dove around here. Those who went to DisCity? Sure they were all nice before. But once they found out they were leaving, did any of them even bother to say goodbye?
Ting-a-ling! Ting-a-ling!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Now, now, Mr. Philippe, let's be fair. We all forget things when we get excited. I'm sure they didn't mean it on purpose.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I'll keep an eye out for your daughter's message. You'll be the first to know if I receive any letters back. Well, I'd better get going. See you around!
Folks who went to DisCity? Letters back? Your ears perk up at these keywords amid the seemingly casual chatter. Deliberately, you move closer toward the ringing sound, trying to follow the leads.

As if the girl truly is a luck bringer, the ringing draws nearer, and soon you spot the source: an old-fashioned bicycle gliding down the lane. Perched on it is Dove, carrying with her a mellow breeze.

She greets every passerby with a warm smile. Her messenger bag sways at her side, offering glimpses of its pristine white interior. Dappled sunlight filters through the green canopy, casting a patchwork of light and shadow over her, like a still from a timeless film.
As you ponder how to broach the subject, Dove spots you first.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Oh, if it isn't Désir's new guest! Have you settled in?
Dove calls out warmly, clumsily stopping her bicycle with her foot, managing to halt just in front of you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, all thanks to you. What are you...?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Can't you tell? I'm a messenger, just doing my daily rounds around. If you ever want to send a message, home letter or invitation, just hit me up!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you ever receive mail from DisCity?
Dove covers her mouth with a soft chuckle and nods.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Of course! Many folks here in Désir have ties far in DisCity; that's why they came here in the first place. So we make sure they can keep in touch!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I see... Looks like this place really is as good as they say.
Though agreeing with her, you sound skeptical. Dove, somehow accustomed to such reaction, pulls out a few letters from her bag, holding them up as if she's done it many times before.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I know what you're worried about, but Désir is truly different! When we say we'll deliver your mail, we mean it. It's not an empty promise.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: See? These are all letters sending back. I'm delivering each one of them, straight into every recipient's hands!

You fan out the letters she gave you and see the different sets of handwriting and signatures on them. The carefully smoothed-out creases and meticulously copied addresses lend credence to Dove's words.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Has anyone who made it to DisCity write back to bring their families over?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've heard Désir helps quite a few people move there. You must have seen letters like that, right?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Hmm not likely... More often than not, by the time I get such a letter, the recipient has already left for DisCity too. A few residents do write letters as soon as they know they're leaving, and ask me to send out later.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: But that's rare because—well, you see, I've never got my turn, I can only dream of it—but from what I hear, people are notified on such short notice that they barely have time to pack, let alone write.
What Dove says piques your interest. Clearly, she knows more than other residents here, and is more willing to share her insights...
Just as you're about to press for more information, an urgent voice cuts in from the distance, interrupting your chat.

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: Dove! Where are you? Has my daughter's letter arrived yet?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Oh my! I must have lost track of time... I'm so sorry! Will be right there!
The call jolts Dove out of the chit-chat. She hastily waves goodbye to you before clambering back onto her bicycle, pedaling away in a rush.
You instinctively wave back, only to realize you're still clutching the letters she handed you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait! I still have your letters!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Sorry...! But I can't turn around here!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Could... could you deliver them for me? They're all addressed! Find street signs at intersections, then the number plates! Thank you—!
Dove's voice is swallowed by the breeze, fading into the distance. You watch her pedal away, struggling to keep her balance while trying to fish letters out of her bag. You let out a small sigh.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Guess she literally has her hands full... Alright, I'll deliver them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Might be a perfect chance to get to know the town's layout and its residents.
